newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs maul Rocard's hours-for-jobs scheme.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs maul Rocard's hours-for-jobs scheme.

text.p: A novel idea for using the money governments currently spend on unemployment benefits to subsidise a drop in working hours - and thus create new jobs - was hacked to bits by Euro-MPs on Wednesday.

Former French Premier Michel Rocard, now a Socialist Euro-MP, had come up with a proposal for tackling the European Union's 20-million-strong dole queues by distributing the number of working hours differently.
Thus instead of employing five people to work eight hours a day, a firm could have eight people working five.

The majority of Euro-MPs saw some value in trying a new approach to unemployment, which costs the EU member states 350 million Ecus a year in social security payments - over four percent of EU gross domestic product.
But Christian-Democrat Euro-MPs objected to Rocard's suggestion that the scheme should be funded using government money.
Rocard said the idea needed to be acceptable both to companies taking on new staff and to workers taking a cut in hours.

He suggested the member states could use the savings they made in their unemployment budgets to compensate workers for loss of wages and subsidise new jobs, either by direct subsidy or by halving employers' social security contributions on the first 32 hours worked and doubling contributions on hours worked after that.

When the European Parliament came to vote on Rocard's proposal, Euro-MPs accepted his idea on employers' contributions but the Christian Democrats succeeded in pushing through amendments which took out all references to government financing and worker compensation.
The Parliament approved the amended proposal by 300 to 59.
They left it to the European Commission to examine whether reducing working hours was a feasible option for reducing unemployment and come up with a viable way of paying for it.
